exposure: Elective induction of labour at 40+0 weeks of gestation
Elective induction of labour at 41+0 weeks of gestation
cohort: Pregnant females aged 20-35 years with parity less than 5, singleton alive pregnancy, and vertex presentation, divided into two groups for elective induction at either 40+0 or 41+0 weeks of gestation.
finding: There was a significantly lower rate of cesarean section in elective induction of labour at 41 weeks as compared to 40 weeks of gestation (12% vs 28%, p=0.046).
mod_finding: The study found a significantly lower rate of cesarean section for elective induction of labour at 41 weeks compared to 40 weeks of gestation.
cross-section timing: During labour induction at 40+0 or 41+0 weeks of gestation, between July and December 2017.
gest_age: 40+0 weeks of gestation, 41+0 weeks of gestation
